senses.gloss: give little or no attention to
fail to do something; leave something undone
senses.learner: to fail to do something, or to leave something undone
examples: She neglected to lock the door when she left.

connotation.why: suggests a duty left undone, against plain 'not do' or 'forget'

senses.gloss: the act of having and controlling property
being controlled by passion or the supernatural
a territory that is controlled by a ruling state
senses.learner: a land or area that is controlled by a ruling country
examples: The island was once a possession of a distant empire.

senses.gloss: the trait of resolutely controlling your own behavior
senses.learner: the quality of firmly keeping control of how you behave
examples: She never lost possession of herself, even when he insulted her.

senses.gloss: (sport) the act of controlling the ball (or puck)
senses.learner: in sport, the act of having control of the ball or puck
examples: Our team kept possession of the ball for most of the game.

senses.gloss: a mania restricted to one thing or idea
senses.learner: a mania about just one thing or idea
examples: Collecting old clocks had become a possession with him.

connotation.why: frames a single interest as a mania, against plain 'interest' or 'passion'
